reads_as_reason: Box head with a large black visor slab, slab chest and pelvis, and shoulder-wide straight arms and legs read as a blocky action-figure or Roblox character, not a tapered adult humanoid.

G1.evidence: Head is a rounded box with no visible neck; chest and pelvis are separate rounded slabs; shoulders are far wider than both references in the equal-height lineup (metrics P3 = 0.40 against band 0.22-0.29, P2a neck fail). Arms splay outward in a wide A shape with no taper. Reads as a character, not a product.

G2.evidence: Silhouette is a stack of slabs: in the front silhouette the chest runs straight into a shallow pinch and then the pelvis block, and the thighs and shanks are parallel columns with only small steps (P8a 0.8905 and P8b 0.946 both fail). Dark joint bands at waist, elbows and knees in the two-tone view are deliberate, but the forms between them do not flow.

G3.evidence: Two-tone view shows warm-white shells over graphite bands at waist, elbows, knees and ankles, a gloss-black visor, and no accent colour. Caveats: the visor is very large and slab-like, the far arm in the 3/4 view reads almost entirely black, and the back view was not toned.

G4.evidence: Head, chest, pelvis, arm and leg segments all use the same small-radius rounded-box section, so the language is consistent. The consistent language is itself boxy, which is what drives the G1 fail.

G6.evidence: Front IoU against the references is 0.5366 (optimus_like) and 0.5688 (atlas_like). In the lineup the shoulders are much wider, the neck is nearly absent, and the arms flare outward where the references hang close to the body. Legs are untapered columns, and the foot is long (P10a 0.213). What matches: head size (P1 pass), hip and knee heights (P6, P7 pass), white shell over black structure, and a black faceless visor.

pairwise.evidence: R1base has a head with a ledge overhang, bulged and tapered-to-a-spike arms, a diamond-shaped hole between the thighs in the front silhouette, and a pinched neck-chest-waist stack with visible gaps. A5 removes these: the silhouette is cleaner, arms are straight, the two-tone render gives deliberate dark bands, and the proportions are calmer. A5 is still a toy-like block figure, but it is the more finished-looking of the two.

top_changes.change: Narrow the shoulder and upper-arm block to a human proportion (about 0.25 H outer width), and lengthen the visible neck. Add a clear, narrower neck column between head and chest so the head stops sitting on the shoulders.

Taper thigh and shank: make the thigh widest at the hip and narrow to the knee, and make the calf wider than the ankle. Pinch the chest-to-waist transition so the chest, waist and pelvis blend as one flowing form instead of three slabs.
top_changes.profile_param: segments[leg_core].stations[knee].w and .d (reduce), stations[ankle].w and .d (reduce); segments[torso].stations[waist].w (blend toward the pelvis width)

top_changes.change: Shorten the foot toward the 0.13-0.17 H band and bring the arms in so they hang closer to the torso as in both references. Check at equal-height lineup, since arm tips run off the panel edge in the current sheet.

notes: Metrics are quoted as given. The failed numerics P2a, P3, P8a, P8b, P10a and S4b are consistent with what I see. The side-view orientation is hard to read: the protruding box on the back (pack) and the box at the heel add ledges to the side profile, and I could not confirm what each is. The back view in the two-tone sheet is untoned grey, so G3 cannot be judged from behind. Arm tips are cropped at the sheet edge in the equal-height lineup. Surface contour lines and dithered edges in the renders are render artefacts, and I did not count them against the design.
